rationale.conceptual: The method is an established MD technique (cascade simulations with ABOP potential, Wigner-Seitz analysis, radial distributions) applied to a particular materials system. While not novel, it requires careful implementation of cell construction, embedding a spherical inclusion, running configurational cascades with specific thermostatting and stopping conditions, and accurate defect counting, which goes beyond a simple textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of multiple stages: building and equilibrating cells (two types), running 900 individual cascade simulations (50 ps each) with parameter sweeps (energies, temperatures), aggregating outputs, computing defect averages, and calculating radial density profiles. This demands robust scripting, handling of many small files, and a reasonable level of orchestration. It is more than a simple sequential script but does not involve exotic tooling.

The execution is a multi-stage pipeline: cell construction, equilibration at three temperatures, running 900 MD cascades, post-processing for WS defect counts and radial profiles.
